contradictions.fact: How to get the NPS overnight permit

claims.says: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or pick up a walk-up permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center or the Glacier Public Service Center.
$10 per person plus a $6 reservation fee
The Blum cross-country zone is not one of the reservable zones, so it is walk-up only through the wilderness information center near Marblemount.

contradictions.why: ACCESS says the permit can be reserved on Recreation.gov (with a reservation fee), while the camp entry says the Blum zone cannot be reserved and is walk-up only.

claims.says: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) via Noisy-Diobsud Wilderness for the approach; summit area at/near the North Cascades National Park boundary.
the park boundary sits close to the river crossing, so assume the whole climb is inside the park

contradictions.why: ACCESS puts the approach in National Forest wilderness with only the summit near the park, while the bivy says to assume the whole climb, from the river crossing up, is inside the park.

contradictions.fact: Where the climbers' path leaves the trail

claims.says: the unmarked climbers' path starting about 175 yards downstream of it on Blum Creek's north bank
leave trail 606 a short distance past the Baker River suspension bridge, before Blum Creek

contradictions.why: The path starts 175 yards downstream of the bridge in one field and a short distance past the bridge in another.

contradictions.fact: Whether the Blum zone permit can be reserved

claims.says: all overnight backcountry stays require a backcountry permit (reserve on Recreation.gov or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center)
Reserve on Recreation.gov, or pick up a walk-up permit in person
Only high-use cross-country zones can be reserved in advance and the Blum zone is not one of them, so the permit is obtained as a walk-up in person
$10/person/night plus a $6 nonrefundable reservation fee

contradictions.why: Two fields say the permit can be reserved on Recreation.gov, while access.permit and every bivy say the Blum zone is walk-up only.
contradictions.internal_resolution: access.permit and all bivy permit notes agree the zone is walk-up only

contradictions.fact: Where the route leaves the Chain Lakes Trail

claims.says: At the last switchback below Herman Saddle ... leave the maintained trail and go cross-country
THE EXIT IS BELOW THE SADDLE, NOT AT IT ... If you crest the saddle ... you have gone past your exit
Chain Lakes Trail is followed to about 4,500 ft, where climbers peel off trail and start up the gully toward Herman Saddle
Above the saddle you leave any trail and work up loose heather benches and talus on Herman's broad south face

contradictions.why: The approach leaves the trail at the last switchback just below the ~5,300-ft saddle and warns that cresting the saddle overshoots, while the waypoints leave the trail at 4,500 ft up a gully and then carry on above the saddle.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, approach_variants, beta, descent_text and the itinerary all use the last-switchback exit

contradictions.fact: Distance to Herman Saddle and the summit

claims.says: At about 0.75 mile, the trail joins Chain Lakes Trail ... toward Herman Saddle (~5,300 ft), roughly 1.5-2 miles and about 1,100 ft above the lakes

contradictions.why: The approach puts the saddle ~2.25-2.75 mi in, and the itinerary gives 6.2 mi round trip, but the waypoints put the saddle at 3.5 mi and the summit at 4.6 mi one way (~9.2 mi round trip).
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, dist_km (6.0 mi) and the itinerary agree on a ~6-mi round trip

trailhead lng -121.682622
